entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:2
segments: A debtor who without his fault is poor, and really not able to pay, should not be imprisoned, nor disabled from making efforts; nor should payment be enforced till he is, or by suitable means may be able to meet it.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:3
segments:
Thy brother; an Israelite. 
 
While we are bound, as we have opportunity and ability, to do good to all who are needy, we are under special obligations to do it to the friends of God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:9
segments: Givest him naught; dost not lend to him what he needs.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:10
segments: The fact that a man is poor and may not be able to repay, is not to prevent us from lending to him, when it is necessary to relieve hs wants and our doing so will be for his benefit; but we are to love our neighbor as ourselves, and do what such love, under the guidance of sound wisdom, requires.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:11
segments: God suffers the poor always to be among us, that compassion may be cultivated by exercise and that we may have opportunity to show whether or not we are disposed to assist them, and thus to imitate our Father in heaven.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:12
segments: If thy brother--be sold unto thee; be bound to serve thee for the payment of a debt, according to the custom of that age.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:14
segments: Liberality to servants and those who have assisted us, and readiness in return to assist them, is an exhibition of excellence, and a source of blessings to both givers and receivers.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:16
segments:
Because he is well with thee; because, in his estimation, it would be better for him to stay than to go away. 
 
It is well so to treat servants as to secure their confidence, gratitude, and esteem, and that they will rather continue with us than go away.  By so doing, their services may be greatly prolonged, and rendered much more pleasant and useful to us and to themselves.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:18
segments:
Worth a double hired servant; because he has served without wages. 
 
Kindness and liberality to servants are means of securing not only their good will and fidelity, but also the blessing of God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 15:22
segments: Within thy gates; at home: not at the tabernacle or temple, as was the case with that which was without blemish.
Fidelity to God, in rendering to him what he requires, is the way to secure his favors, and make them the means of the greatest enjoyment to ourselves and others.
